attack_anchor.title: Simple Power Analysis Attack on SQIsign
attack_anchor.relevance: The published attack targets a secret-derived exponent used by modular square root inside Cornacchia and connects exponent recovery to signing-key recovery.

threat_model.temporary_modulus: The Cornacchia modular-square-root modulus M is secret-derived on the signing route. It must not be treated as a public Montgomery modulus without a separate proof.
observations: value-based leakage from registers, ALU operands/results, loads, stores and spills
transition-based leakage between consecutive values on registers, buses and memory paths
horizontal observations across the 521 repeated exponent rounds in one trace
multi-call observations across the several exponentiations used by one modular-square-root invocation
threat_model.scope_boundary: This source-level model identifies values that a countermeasure must cover. It does not prove that any one value is externally observable on RP2350, nor that masking is the only possible countermeasure.

primary_masking_literature.title: On the Cost of Lazy Engineering for Masked Software Implementations
primary_masking_literature.relevance: Separates value-based from transition-based leakage and shows why source-level share marginals do not suffice.
primary_masking_literature.not_a_drop_in: It does not provide masked SQIsign or masked dynamic-modulus Montgomery arithmetic.

primary_masking_literature.title: Bitslicing Arithmetic/Boolean Masking Conversions for Fun and Profit
primary_masking_literature.relevance: Provides composable arithmetic/Boolean masking gadgets and demonstrates that plain-C share transitions can create first-order leakage on a Cortex-M4-class target.
primary_masking_literature.not_a_drop_in: Its small-modulus lattice-KEM conversions do not cover 521-bit secret dynamic moduli, Montgomery context generation or SQIsign Tonelli--Shanks state.

primary_masking_literature.title: Threshold Implementations in Software: Micro-architectural Leakages in Algorithms
primary_masking_literature.relevance: Makes final share placement and micro-architectural transitions part of the security argument on scalar embedded processors.
primary_masking_literature.not_a_drop_in: Its symmetric gadgets are not a masked big-integer Montgomery implementation.

current_implementation.interpretation: The fixed schedule removes one control-flow channel but does not hide the values or transitions of the secret-derived modulus, exponent, Montgomery constants or arithmetic state.

rejected_partial_candidates.reason: Constant work and addresses do not imply constant power.
It leaves the exponent words, secret modulus/context and exponent-prefix-dependent arithmetic state unshared; a naive sequential two-share selector also leaks under the frozen HD model.
It leaves the secret modulus/context and arithmetic values exposed, and the checked E=e+r*(M-1) candidate retains exploitable multi-call algebraic structure.
Every reduction still combines shared state with unshared modulus words and the unshared Montgomery inverse; exponent and selector surfaces also remain.
It leaves the exponent, selector and exponent-prefix-dependent Montgomery operands/results exposed.
It leaves the secret-derived modulus, exponent, selector and reduction state exposed.

required_end_to_end_scope: Represent the temporary modulus and every derived Montgomery constant under a reviewed sharing or independently validated hiding discipline before they enter arithmetic.

Use composable gadgets for 521-bit addition, subtraction, comparison/selection, schoolbook multiplication, Montgomery reduction and arithmetic/Boolean conversion; account for carry, borrow and reduction-factor state.

Protect exponent storage, bit extraction, selector logic, base/radicand conversion, accumulator prefixes and final unmasking; no secret-dependent value may be silently reintroduced at an API boundary.
Extend the protection through Tonelli--Shanks setup, repeated powers, state updates, retries, status handling and the Cornacchia consumer rather than approving an isolated pow call.
Freeze final Cortex-M33 assembly and verify share separation across registers, spills, ALU and memory transitions for each compiler build.
Account for fresh randomness, refresh boundaries, failure behavior, zeroization, SRAM and cycle overhead without reusing masks across repeated horizontal observations.
Require first- and higher-order leakage assessment plus attack-driven exponent/modulus/state recovery on independent physical sessions; a negative TVLA alone is not approval.
claim_boundary: This contract proves only that the frozen source directly manipulates a connected set of secret-derived Montgomery values and that six partial countermeasure scopes leave named nodes uncovered. It is not a leakage measurement, probing-security proof, masked implementation or impossibility result for masking/hiding.
